title: DRAFT — web-sourced eponym heads (PARTIAL, 10 heads)
description: UN-APPLIED DRAFT PROPOSAL. Ten head-only eponym attributions, each with a first-hand web (Wikipedia / chess.com / chessable) 'named after / named for / eponym / name attached to' attestation. Graded PARTIAL because the reached sources are web/Wikipedia, NOT reference-grade: each NEEDS A REFERENCE-GRADE PIN (Oxford Companion entry / monograph) to lift to CLEAR before any --strict --apply. The engine's --strict mode REJECTS this manifest on the first PARTIAL grade (by design). HEAD ROWS ONLY - no child rows. Review notes carried per head: B.Fre.Mac spelling discrepancy (person 'McCutcheon' vs catalogue variation 'MacCutcheon'); C.KGm.Acc.Kie first described by Polerio (16th c.), named after Kieseritzky for his 5.Ne5 theory; B.Fre.Win was previously mis-graded CLEAR on a debunked 'The Center Game' source - now correctly PARTIAL on Wikipedia. NOT for the live manifests dir; inert draft.

source_refs: Wikipedia, 'French Defence' - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Defence : 'The Winawer Variation, named after Szymon Winawer and pioneered by Aron Nimzowitsch and Mikhail Botvinnik, is one of the main systems in the French.' WEB-ONLY; needs reference-grade pin. CORRECTION: the prior CLEAR rested on 'The Center Game' (Arne Moll's monograph on the Center Game, a DIFFERENT opening); that NotebookLM grounding was hallucinated and is debunked - do not cite it.

fields.historical_notes: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Bb4. The Winawer Variation, named after Szymon Winawer (1838-1919) and pioneered by Aron Nimzowitsch and Mikhail Botvinnik. The same eponym also names the Winawer Countergambit in the Slav (catalogue D.Sla.Win) - a distinct line. Head row only.
